hero.headline: Learn to see problems differently. Learn to create solutions.
hero.text: The Problem-Solving Experience is powered by Edunotech. It helps students develop observation, critical thinking, creativity, and practical problem-solving capabilities through guided learning and the purposeful application of technology.

what.heading: It starts with a different way of thinking.
paragraphs: Many problems remain unresolved not because solutions are impossible, but because people have not taken the time to observe, question, and understand them properly.
The Problem-Solving Experience introduces students to a more deliberate approach to thinking and action.

Participants learn to notice what could be better, investigate why a challenge exists, understand who is affected, generate possible ideas, assess their relevance, and explore how practical solutions can be developed.
Technology becomes part of this process where it is useful. It is not automatically treated as the answer to every problem.
The goal is to help students become more observant, thoughtful, creative, and responsible problem solvers.

principles.quote: A problem that is well understood is 50% solved.
principles.text: This is an Edunotech guiding principle, not a scientific measurement. It means careful investigation and understanding are the foundation for any meaningful solution.

principles.quote: The problem determines the tool, not the other way around.
principles.text: The right solution should emerge from the needs of the problem. Sometimes technology is necessary. Sometimes a simpler, non-digital approach is more appropriate.

framework.title: Feeling
framework.text: Recognising that something could be better or that an unmet need may exist.

framework.title: Observation
framework.text: Paying attention to people, environments, behaviour, processes, and recurring difficulties.

framework.title: Understanding
framework.text: Investigating what is happening, why it happens, and who is affected.

framework.title: Ideation
framework.text: Generating possible approaches and exploring different ways to address the problem.

framework.title: Idea Filtering
framework.text: Evaluating ideas based on relevance, feasibility, impact, cost, resources, and sustainability.

framework.title: Validation
framework.text: Testing whether the problem and proposed solution are supported by evidence and real user needs.

framework.title: Solution Design
framework.text: Choosing an appropriate approach and planning how it can work.

framework.title: Execution
framework.text: Developing, testing, improving, and implementing the solution.

framework.title: Impact
framework.text: Assessing the value created and identifying opportunities for improvement.

technology.heading: Technology should serve the solution.
paragraphs: Participants explore how technology can help them investigate problems, develop ideas, and create solutions.
Depending on the challenge, this may involve artificial intelligence, coding, software development, digital design, data, automation, cybersecurity, or other emerging technologies.
They also learn that responsible technology use requires independent thinking, verification, privacy awareness, and an understanding of limitations.

audience.heading: Who is it for?
paragraphs: The primary audience is students in tertiary institutions across different academic disciplines.

The experience is not restricted to students studying Computer Science, engineering, or other technology-related courses. Students from education, health sciences, business, social sciences, arts, sciences, and other disciplines can relate the framework to challenges within their own environments.
The programme may also be adapted for other learning environments and audiences.

outcomes: The ability to investigate problems rather than make assumptions
An understanding of how to validate needs and proposed solutions
Better judgement when selecting tools and approaches
Confidence in developing and presenting solutions
An increased sense of responsibility towards solving real problems

institutional.heading: Bring the Problem-Solving Experience to Your Institution.
paragraphs: Edunotech welcomes conversations with universities, polytechnics, colleges of education, and other institutions interested in helping students develop practical problem-solving and technology capabilities.
The experience can be adapted to institutional needs, student populations, available resources, and preferred delivery formats.
